{{Short description|Finite simple group; sometimes classed as sporadic}}
{{pp-semi-indef}}
{{Group theory sidebar |Finite}}

In [[group theory]], 
the '''Tits group''' <sup>2</sup>''F''<sub>4</sub>(2)′, named for  [[Jacques Tits]] ({{IPA|fr|tits|lang}}), is a finite [[simple group]] of [[Order (group theory)|order]]
:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;17,971,200 = 2<sup>11</sup>&nbsp;·&nbsp;3<sup>3</sup>&nbsp;·&nbsp;5<sup>2</sup>&nbsp;·&nbsp;13.

This is the only simple group that is a [[derived group|derivative]] of a [[group of Lie type]] that is not a group of Lie type in any series from exceptional isomorphisms. It is sometimes considered a 27th [[sporadic group]].

==History and properties==
The [[Ree groups]] <sup>2</sup>''F''<sub>4</sub>(2<sup>2''n''+1</sup>) were constructed by {{harvtxt|Ree|1961}}, who showed that they are simple if ''n''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;1. The first member <sup>2</sup>''F''<sub>4</sub>(2) of this series is not simple. It was studied by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Jacques Tits|first=Jacques|last= Tits|year=1964}} who showed that it is [[almost simple group|almost simple]], its [[derived subgroup]] <sup>2</sup>''F''<sub>4</sub>(2)′ of index&nbsp;2 being a new simple group, now called the Tits group. The group <sup>2</sup>''F''<sub>4</sub>(2) is a [[group of Lie type]] and has a [[BN pair]], but the Tits group itself does not have a BN pair. The Tits group is member of the infinite family <sup>2</sup>''F''<sub>4</sub>(2<sup>2''n''+1</sup>)′ of commutator groups of the Ree groups, and thus by definition not sporadic. But because it is also not strictly a group of Lie type, it is sometimes regarded as a 27th [[sporadic group]].<ref>For instance, by the [[ATLAS of Finite Groups]] and its [http://brauer.maths.qmul.ac.uk/Atlas/v3/spor/ web-based descendant]</ref>

The [[Schur multiplier]] of the Tits group is trivial and its [[outer automorphism group]] has order&nbsp;2, with the full automorphism group being the group&nbsp;<sup>2</sup>''F''<sub>4</sub>(2).

The Tits group occurs as a maximal subgroup of the [[Fischer group Fi22|Fischer group Fi<sub>22</sub>]]. The group <sup>2</sup>''F''<sub>4</sub>(2) also occurs as a maximal subgroup of the [[Rudvalis group]], as the point stabilizer of the [[rank-3 permutation action]] on 4060&nbsp;=&nbsp;1&nbsp;+&nbsp;1755&nbsp;+&nbsp;2304 points.

The Tits group is one of the [[N-group (finite group theory)|simple N-groups]], and was not included in [[John G. Thompson]]'s first announcement of the classification of simple ''N''-groups, as it had not been discovered at the time. It is also one of the [[thin finite group]]s.

The Tits group was characterized in various ways by {{harvs|txt|last=Parrott|year1=1972|year2=1973}} and {{harvtxt|Stroth|1980}}.

==Presentation==
The Tits group can be defined in terms of generators and relations by

:<math>a^2 = b^3 = (ab)^{13} = [a, b]^5 = [a, bab]^4 = ((ab)^4 ab^{-1})^6 = 1, \,</math>

where [''a'',&nbsp;''b''] is the [[commutator]] ''a''<sup>−1</sup>''b''<sup>−1</sup>''ab''. It has an [[outer automorphism]] obtained by sending (''a'',&nbsp;''b'') to (''a'',&nbsp;''b''(''ba'')<sup>5</sup>''b''(''ba'')<sup>5</sup>).
